prompt: i have 6 sweets and amma gives me 2 more
reply:
Six are already in your hand. 🍬 Now two more arrive. 🤲 Start at six and hop up twice. Which number do you land on?
[CHIPS]Eight sweets|Hop with me|Try adding three[/CHIPS]

prompt: amma gave me 10 grapes and i ate 4
reply:
Ten fingers up for the grapes. 🍇 Now fold four down for the ones you ate. Six fingers are still standing, so six grapes are left. 🖐️
[CHIPS]Eat two more|Show me again|Try twelve grapes[/CHIPS]

prompt: we cut one roti into 4 pieces and 2 of us eat one piece each
reply:
Picture the roti in four pieces. 🫓 Two friends take one piece each. That is two gone. How many wait on the plate? 😋
[CHIPS]Two pieces|Draw the roti|Cut into six[/CHIPS]

prompt: my dog has 4 puppies how many puppy ears are there
reply:
Every puppy has two ears. 🐶 Count in twos with me. Where do you stop? 🐾
[POEM]Four little puppies in a row, two ears each, now count them slow.[/POEM]
[CHIPS]I stopped at eight|Count with me|Try six puppies[/CHIPS]

prompt: 5 birds were on the wire and 3 flew away
reply:
[BIG]🐦[/BIG]
Three flew off, so fold three fingers down from five. Two birds are still sitting on the wire. 👀 Taking some away always leaves you with fewer than you started.
[CHIPS]Add two birds|Do it again|Try eight birds[/CHIPS]

prompt: appa gave me 2 rupees and thatha gave me 5 rupees
reply:
Push both piles together first. 🪙 Two coins, then five coins. Count the whole pile out loud. How many rupees now? 😃
[CHIPS]Seven rupees|Count out loud|Add one rupee[/CHIPS]

prompt: i have 3 toy cars and my friend has 3 toy cars
reply:
Three and three is a doubles sum, and doubles are the quickest sums to learn by heart. 🚗 Three fingers on each hand makes six, so between you there are six toy cars. ✋
[CHIPS]What are doubles|Try four plus four|Now double six[/CHIPS]

prompt: amma made 8 idlis for me and my brother to share
reply:
Sharing means fair, so both plates must end up the same. 🍚 Deal them out one at a time and each plate fills up with four idlis. 🍽️
[STEPS]One idli for you|One for your brother|Both plates reach four[/STEPS]
[CHIPS]Try six idlis|Deal them again|Add two idlis[/CHIPS]

prompt: i put 2 flowers in each of my 3 cups
reply:
Two in the first cup. Two in the next. 🌸 One more cup to go. Count in twos out loud! 🌼
[POEM]Two by two the flowers grow, three small cups all in a row.[/POEM]
[CHIPS]Six flowers|Count in twos|Use four cups[/CHIPS]

prompt: there were 7 mangoes and a monkey took 1
reply:
One less than seven. 🐒 Say the counting numbers backwards. Seven, then what comes next? That one is your answer. 🥭
[CHIPS]Six mangoes|Say it backwards|Monkey takes two[/CHIPS]

prompt: my bag had 4 books and i put 2 more inside
reply:
Start at four in your head, then hop two steps up: five, six. 🎒 That lands you on six books. Hopping on from the bigger number beats counting from one every time. 📚
[CHIPS]Why start at four|Put in three more|Try nine books[/CHIPS]

prompt: 10 ants were walking and 5 went into the hole
reply:
Ten ants marching. 🐜 Five went in, so that is half. Half stays outside in the sun. 🌿
[QUIZ]How many ants are still marching?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]Five ants|Ten ants|Two ants[/CHIPS]

prompt: i had 9 crayons and lost 2 of them
reply:
Count backwards two steps from nine. 🖍️ Eight is step one. What is step two? Try it on your fingers. 🤔
[CHIPS]Seven crayons|Count back again|Lose one more[/CHIPS]

prompt: if 4 friends share 20 laddus equally how many does each one get
reply:
Sharing equally is just dealing cards. One laddu each uses up 4, a second round makes 8 gone, and by the fifth round all 20 are dealt. 🍥 Five rounds means five laddus each. 😋
[CHIPS]Try 24 laddus|Show the rounds|What if 5 friends[/CHIPS]

prompt: one bus ticket costs 12 rupees how much for 3 people
reply:
Three tickets means three lots of 12. Split the 12 into 10 and 2, because those are friendlier. 🚌 Three tens is thirty, so now work out three twos and add them on. That splitting trick is how most people do maths in their head. 🎟️
[CHIPS]Thirty six rupees|Show the split|Four tickets now[/CHIPS]

prompt: india scored 156 and needs 200 how many more runs
reply:
How-far-to-go questions are subtraction, but hopping is easier. Hop from 156 up to 160 first, which is 4 runs. 🏏 Then hop from 160 to 200. Add your two hops together and you have the runs still needed. 🙌
[CHIPS]Forty four runs|Show the hops|What about 180[/CHIPS]

prompt: i bought a pencil for 15 rupees and gave a 50 rupee note
reply:
Shopkeepers count up, never down, and it is far easier on your head. ✏️ From 15 you jump 5 to reach 20, then 30 more to reach 50. Those two jumps together are your change: 35 rupees. 💰
[STEPS]15 plus 5 is 20|20 plus 30 is 50|Change is 5 plus 30[/STEPS]
[CHIPS]Buy two pencils|Pay with 100|Why count up[/CHIPS]

prompt: amma cut 4 rotis into 6 pieces each and there are 4 of us
reply:
Two-step problem, so do not rush at one answer. 🫓 Find the total pieces first, then share that total out. Tell me the total before we split it. 🍽️
[STEPS]6 pieces per roti|4 rotis altogether|Share the total among 4[/STEPS]
[CHIPS]Total is 24|Six pieces each|Try six rotis[/CHIPS]

prompt: there are 5 rows of plants and 8 plants in every row
reply:
Rows and columns make an array, which is repeated addition in a tidy grid. 🌱 Skip count the eights: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. The garden holds 40 plants, and eight fives gets you to the same place faster. 🧠
[FACT]Multiplication works in any order: 5 x 8 equals 8 x 5.[/FACT]
[CHIPS]Add one row|Skip count fives|Try 6 rows[/CHIPS]

prompt: i have 45 rupees and each comic costs 20 rupees
reply:
Keep subtracting 20 until you cannot any more. 45 minus 20 leaves 25. 📚 Take another 20, and see what is left now. When the leftover is smaller than 20 you stop and count the comics. 🧮
[CHIPS]Two comics|Five rupees left|Try 65 rupees[/CHIPS]

prompt: our class has 32 students sitting in pairs how many desks do we need
reply:
Pairs means groups of two, so this is really halving. Break 32 into friendly chunks: half of 30, then half of 2, and add those halves. 🪑 Chunking makes halving big numbers feel easy. 🙂
[QUIZ]So how many desks does the class need?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]16 desks|32 desks|8 desks[/CHIPS]

prompt: one dosa costs 25 rupees how much will 4 dosas cost
reply:
Think in coins: two 25s make 50, and two 50s make 100. 🪙 So four dosas cost 100 rupees, and you got there by doubling twice instead of adding 25 over and over. 🍽️
[FACT]Doubling a number twice is the same as multiplying by four.[/FACT]
[CHIPS]Six dosas now|Show the doubling|What about eight[/CHIPS]

prompt: the train leaves at 3 o clock and takes 2 hours 30 minutes
reply:
Time adds in chunks, never all in one go. Add the whole hours first: 3 o'clock plus 2 hours. 🚂 Then drop the 30 minutes on top of that. Say the arrival time out loud and see whether it sounds right. ⏰
[CHIPS]Half past five|Add three hours|Start at four[/CHIPS]

prompt: i scored 18 runs and 24 runs in two matches what is my average
reply:
Average asks a fair question: if both innings had been equal, what would each one be? 🏏 Pour the runs together, 18 plus 24 is 42, then split that across your 2 matches. Your average is 21 runs. 🙌
[CHIPS]Add a third score|Why divide by two|Try 30 and 40[/CHIPS]

prompt: a packet has 12 biscuits and i want to share with my 2 friends
reply:
The sneaky bit here is counting yourself. You plus 2 friends makes 3 people, not 2. 🍪 So split 12 into 3 equal piles instead. How many biscuits land in each pile? 🤔
[CHIPS]Four each|I forgot myself|Share 15 biscuits[/CHIPS]

prompt: auto to school costs 30 rupees each way how much for 5 days
reply:
Start small: one day is two rides, there and back, so 60 rupees a day. 🛺 Five days is five lots of 60, which comes to 300 rupees for the week. Building up from a single day keeps the numbers friendly. 🗓️
[CHIPS]What about 6 days|Only one way|Try 40 rupees[/CHIPS]

prompt: a shopkeeper buys 40 notebooks at 18 rupees each and sells each at 25
reply:
Two routes, same destination, so pick the one with the smaller numbers. Route A is total sales minus total cost, 1000 minus 720. 📒 Route B is profit per notebook, 25 minus 18, times 40. Both land on 280 rupees, and when two routes disagree the slip is almost always in the bigger multiplication.
[CHIPS]Show route A|Add shop costs|Try selling at 22[/CHIPS]

prompt: a phone is 15000 rupees with 20 percent off what do i actually pay
reply:
Careful: the discount is what you do not pay, so the amount you hand over is 80 percent. Anchor on 10 percent, which is 1500 here. 📱 Double that for the discount, or multiply it by 8 to jump straight to what you pay. Both routes must land on the same number.
[FACT]Percent comes from Latin per centum, meaning by the hundred.[/FACT]
[CHIPS]I pay 12000|Show the 80% route|Try 30% off[/CHIPS]

prompt: a car covers 240 km in 3 hours what is the speed
reply:
Speed is distance shared out over one single hour, so it is 240 divided by 3, giving 80 km per hour. 🚗 Now run it backwards: 80 times 3 is 240, right back where you started. That reverse check catches nearly every arithmetic slip.
[FACT]A speed always pairs a distance with a time.[/FACT]
[CHIPS]Now find the time|Try 300 in 4|Why check backwards[/CHIPS]

prompt: 2 taps fill a tank in 6 hours how long would 3 taps take
reply:
Resist multiplying, because more taps means less time and that makes this an inverse problem. Find the single-tap rate first: if 2 taps need 6 hours, one tap alone needs 12. 💧 Now split that 12-hour job across 3 taps. Sanity check: your answer has to come out under 6 hours.
[CHIPS]Four hours|Why inverse|Try four taps[/CHIPS]

prompt: i cycled 5 km in 20 minutes what is that in km per hour
reply:
Units must match before you divide, because minutes and hours cannot share a fraction line. 🚴 Twenty minutes is one third of an hour, so a whole hour covers three times 5 km, which is 15 km per hour.
[STEPS]20 minutes is one third|That third covers 5 km|A whole hour covers 15[/STEPS]
[CHIPS]Try 10 minutes|Explain the thirds|Now in metres[/CHIPS]

prompt: a rice recipe for 4 people uses 300 grams how much for 7 people
reply:
Scale through the unit: grams for one person. 300 divided by 4 gives one share, then multiply that by 7. 🍚 Estimate before you compute, though. Seven is a little under double four, so expect a little under 600 grams, and if your answer sits there you are almost certainly right.
[CHIPS]525 grams|Show unit method|Scale to ten[/CHIPS]

prompt: the ticket is 250 rupees with 40 percent student discount
reply:
Two answers hide in this one question: what you save and what you pay. 10 percent of 250 is 25, and the discount is four of those. 🎟️ So you save 100 and hand over 150. Saving plus payment rebuilds 250, which is the check built into the problem.
[CHIPS]Show the check|Try 15% off|Why four lots[/CHIPS]

prompt: in a class of 40 students 60 percent play cricket how many do not
reply:
Read it twice, because it asks for the students who do not play. Shortcut: if 60 percent play, 40 percent do not, so work with 40 directly. 🏏 Ten percent of 40 is 4, and you scale up from there. The long way, finding 24 and subtracting, must give the identical number.
[CHIPS]Sixteen students|Both ways agree|Make it 75%[/CHIPS]

prompt: i save 150 rupees every month how long to buy a 2400 rupee bat
reply:
This is really asking how many 150s fit inside 2400. 🏏 Chunking beats long division when the numbers are this friendly: ten months banks 1500, which leaves 900, and 900 needs six more months. Sixteen months of saving buys the bat.
[STEPS]Ten months makes 1500|900 left to cover|Six more months clears it[/STEPS]
[CHIPS]Save 200 monthly|Show the chunks|What about 3000[/CHIPS]

prompt: our garden is 12 metres by 8 metres how much fence and how much grass
reply:
Two different measurements, so keep them firmly apart. Fence runs around the edge: 12 plus 8 plus 12 plus 8 is 40 metres of perimeter. 🌿 Grass covers the inside: 12 times 8 is 96 square metres of area. If both your answers carry the same unit, you have mixed the two up.
[FACT]Perimeter is a plain length; area is always in square units.[/FACT]
[CHIPS]Add a path|Try 10 by 10|Why square metres[/CHIPS]

prompt: my brother and i split 350 rupees in the ratio 3 to 4
reply:
Ratios work in parts, not rupees, so count the parts first: 3 plus 4. 💰 Divide 350 by that total to find what a single part is worth, then multiply back by 3 and by 4. The two shares must add to 350, and that is how you know you are right.
[CHIPS]150 and 200|What is one part|Try 2 to 5[/CHIPS]

prompt: we need 72 runs in 6 overs what run rate do we need
reply:
Required run rate is simply the runs left divided by the overs left, so 72 over 6. 🏏 Then ask the question a captain actually asks: is that rate realistic against this bowling? Maths hands you a number, judgement decides what to do with it.
[QUIZ]So what rate do the last 6 overs need?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]12 an over|6 an over|18 an over[/CHIPS]

prompt: a shirt was 800 rupees and now it is 640 what percent is off
reply:
Percentage change always compares the drop to the original price, never to the new one. Find the drop first: 800 minus 640. 👕 Then ask what fraction that drop is of 800 and turn it into a percentage. Handy anchor: 10 percent of 800 is 80, so count how many 80s fit.
[CHIPS]Twenty percent|Show the fraction|What if 600[/CHIPS]

prompt: if i mix 2 litres of juice with 3 litres of water how much juice is in 10 litres
reply:
The mix totals 5 litres and 2 of those are juice, so juice is two fifths of any batch you make. 🧃 Ten litres is double five litres, so every ingredient doubles too: 4 litres of juice and 6 of water. They add back to 10, which is your check.
[CHIPS]Show two fifths|Scale to fifteen|Make it sweeter[/CHIPS]
